      "complete_original_UTF8_body": "# Actual real phase growth and the remaining beyond-square-root HS gap

UNFROZEN AUTHOR WORKING / BOUNDED FEASIBILITY, NOT A COEFFICIENT RESULT.
EM-PUBLIC-7CDA51, actual45/133 with original actual Source-specific
startup/checkpoint exit0/debt[]/fiveformalfalse. This later work does not
change the fixed94793-byte many-row whole or inherit a future peer vote.

import/AST/test or budget reset. Old STOP/HOLD/NONBLIND/UNKNOWN remain.

This note gives two derived model-specific bounds and an honest terminal
comparison. It is one piece of the new beyond-square-root feasibility,
not a standalone paper/Tool or a positive coefficient conclusion. BFF's
new B9051 and 883's conditional real-row restoration are separate actual
author inputs; their mathematics is not silently declared peer accepted.

## 1. Precise old inputs and what is newly derived

Use integer m>=2^1000, N=m-1, M=m-1/2. Let n be the largest even
integer<=m-2, t=m-n in{2,3}, ell=n-1, Hn=n!sqrt(h0/hn),
Cxi=Hn/(2pi)^n, An(a)=Cxi a^ell and Chat=pi^ell Cxi.
Keep the SAME Student degree<=m-2 carrier and actual positive adjoint.

The genuinely accepted98b1f4b3075da2afab249b85375e73f883ae710e real-state
primary, with genuine peer88c190aba4414288c908a43ece9abec138ae742d, proves
in its exact finite-coefficient section3 that, on positive real z,

 E_m(z):=A_M(z)^2+B_M(z)^2
   =sum_(r=0)^N [c_(N,r)/c_(N,N)] z^(2(N-r)),
 c_(N,r)=(N+r)!/(N-r)! *binom(2r,r)/4^r,
 A_M=-pi(z/2)^M Y_M/Gamma(M),
 B_M= pi(z/2)^M J_M/Gamma(M).                         (E1)

The exact positive finite formula is reused, not just its weakened
E_m>=1 conclusion. I personally previously whole-read/bound that actual
source and genuine peer, and now targeted-reread section3 in full. No new
external primary HTTP or new asymptotic theorem is claimed. Its old
final coefficient range is not extended by the old verdict.

The accepted031d516fcbb1679ec804ec34b3c3cf5b8df8a923 with genuine peer
3b3461946201c1ea3a58646579a6f0304db8bf00 contains the ambient finite
translation/Laplace proof and exact norm comparison. Its old working
N5--N17 is also genuinely personally whole-read; the targeted N8--N15
algebra was reread here. The natural constant bound had |z|<=sqrt(N)/4.
Below I retain the exponential that the old proof bounded by a constant;
this is a NEW derivation, not an extension of its old final verdict.

## 2. A true growing lower bound for the actual common phase energy

Reindex (E1) by s=N-r and put a_(m,s)=c_(N,N-s)/c_(N,N).
Then a_(m,0)=1 and direct factorial division, for1<=s<=m-1, gives

 a_(m,s)/a_(m,s-1)
   =(2m-2s)/[s(2m-2s-1)(2m-s-1)]
   >=1/(2m s).                                         (E2)

All denominators are positive on this EXACT finite support. The last
inequality uses (2m-2s)/(2m-2s-1)>1 and 2m-s-1<2m.
Finite induction yields a_(m,s)>=1/[s!(2m)^s]. For lambda=z^2/(2m),

 E_m(z)>=sum_(s=0)^N lambda^s/s!
        >=(1+lambda/N)^N.                              (E3)

The second inequality follows coefficient by coefficient from
binom(N,s)/N^s<=1/s!: no infinite sum was substituted for the finite
positive polynomial. If 0<=lambda<=N, then log(1+x)>=x/(1+x)>=x/2
at x=lambda/N in[0,1]. Consequently

 E_m(z)>=exp[z^2/(4m)],
                         0<=z^2<=2m(m-1).              (E4)

In particular this holds on pi<=z<=m/128. It is genuine real phase
growth, rather than the old constant lower1. It is not positivity of
an analytic energy at complex z.

If separately |B_M|<=1/2 at the SAME real z, then E_m>=1 implies
A_M^2=E_m-B_M^2>=3E_m/4. Thus

       |A_M|>=sqrt(3)/2 *exp[z^2/(8m)].                  (E5)

The implication is exact. BFF's later B9051 claims a much stronger
linear-z tiny bound; I do not claim its body personally read before it
is actually consumed. No A-near1 hypothesis was used in (E4)--(E5).

## 3. Reprove the full-modulus amplitude where the old natural domain ends

Let 1<=Z<=m/128 be a real modulus. The old monic-minimum/moment argument
gives hn/h0<=4^-n, so

 An(pi/Z)>=n!/(pi Z^(n-1))
          >=(Z/pi)[n/(3Z)]^n,
                       since n!>=(n/3)^n.               (E6)

Here n>=m/2 and n/(3Z)>=64/3>16, while Z/pi>=1/4. Hence
An(pi/Z)>16^n/4>=m^6 at m>=2^1000: 4n-2>=2m-2 and
6log2(m)<=6m/16<2m-2. This is a genuine new wider-domain amplitude
comparison; I have not applied the old sqrt-domain conclusion outside
its statement. It holds at the modulus of complex z as well.

## 4. A rigorous wider-strip upper bound, still with its exponential loss

For complex z with 1<=Z=|z|<=m/128, gamma=|Im z|<=1, set
mu=2Z, phi=-arg z and T=N/(8Z). Then T>=8>1. The old ambient
circle proof, used only as an upper bound on the ACTUAL restriction,
gives for translation of modulus u>=1

 ||exp(u exp(i phi)Dv)||HS,actual
       <=2m^(1/4) rho(u exp(i phi))^N,
 rho^N<=(2u)^N exp[N|sin phi|/(2u)+N/(4u^2)].             (E7)

For every u>=0 the coarse bound is sqrt(m)rho^N, and rho is
nondecreasing along this fixed direction. These algebraic inequalities
were proved before imposing the old z-domain. Since |sin phi|=gamma/Z,
for u>=T their true bounds are

 N|sin phi|/(2u)<=4,
 N/(4u^2)<=16Z^2/N.

Thus, with F=exp[4+16Z^2/N], rho^N<=(2u)^N F. Do not set F to e^5:
16Z^2/N need NOT be<=1 in the present new domain.

The finite nilpotent Laplace identity is

 Tcal=integral_0^infinity e^-v
              (exp(vDv/(2z))+exp(-vDv/(2z)))/2 dv,
 U1(pi/z)=(z/pi)(Tcal-I).                               (E8)

Only finitely many matrix coefficients are integrated termwise. The
ordinary HS triangle inequality and mu=2Z give the same scalar integral
as the old proof. On u>=T, (E7) yields

 I_tail<=2F m^(1/4)Gamma(m)/Z^N.

On0<=u<=T, monotonicity plus the coarse bound gives
I_early<=F sqrt(m)(N/(4Z))^N. Define
G=m^(1/4)Gamma(m)/Z^N. The finite factorial lower N!>=(N/3)^N gives

 I_early/G<=F m^(1/4)(3/4)^N<=F,
                     ||Tcal||HS,actual<=3F G.            (E9)

The final elementary inequality is the same m>=2^1000 comparison as
in the old proof; its cancellation is independent of Z.

The exact accepted Student/Gamma/binomial norm comparison supplies

 An(pi/Z)>=2^-6 m^(1/4)Gamma(m)/Z^(n-1)                   (E10)

for every positive Z; the comparison itself had no small-Z restriction.
Insert (E9)--(E10) into (E8). The actual identity HS is sqrt(m-1),
not1 or an operator norm. By (E6), its normalized contribution is

 sqrt(m-1) Z/[pi An(pi/Z)]<=Z^(1-t),

because sqrt(m)Z^t<=m^(7/2)<pi m^6. Since pi>3 and e<3, choosing
a conservative uniform constant gives the full new bound

 ||U1(pi/z)||HS/An(pi/|z|)
   <=2^18 |z|^(1-t) exp[16|z|^2/(m-1)],
          1<=|z|<=m/128, |Im z|<=1.                     (E11)

This is an actual full-carrier complex upper bound with both parity
blocks and odd top; the ambient space was never substituted for the
actual space. It is a new explicit LOSSY extension of the old bound.
No claim of constant relative control beyond sqrt(m) is made.

not to discard the real A_M amplitude in future state lower bounds.
The B/Y finite-row restoration should retain this amplitude if it is
later needed. BFF/883's linear-z components remain their own conditional
author proofs until fully consumed and integrated, not accepted inputs.

However, squaring (E11) has the upper exponent32Z^2/(m-1), whereas
(E4) supplies only a lower exponent z^2/(4m). These particular sufficient
bounds still leave an exponential quotient. They do NOT themselves give
a constant or polynomial relative local envelope once z^2/m greatly
exceeds log m. This observation concerns the LOSS OF THE CERTIFICATE,
not an actual lower bound on the relative HS norm and not a sign
counterexample. Stronger actual state growth could change the quotient.

In particular no proof is supplied here that a single constant-output
row, even with its real common phase energy retained, captures the
whole HS norm in this larger domain. Other output rows have varying
high orders m-r-1/2; the old fixed-M lemma cannot be applied to them
without an actual parameter/domain proof. Nor do we replace the actual
coherent row/fullmatrix sum by independent positive pole energies.

## 2. Exact entire series and the absolute exponential majorant

Let gamma=M+1=m+1/2. From the J series,

 B_M(z)=pi(z/2)^(2m-1)/[Gamma(M)Gamma(M+1)]
           *sum_(k>=0) (-z^2/4)^k/[k!(m+1/2)_k].             (B4)

For z>0 there is no branch ambiguity: all powers in(B2) use the
positive real value, Gamma(M),Gamma(M+1)>0, and their product
gives exactly the INTEGER exponent2m-1 in(B4). The Pochhammer
parameter m+1/2 is positive, so no denominator vanishes.

The coefficient ratio proves that the last series is entire.
Thus(B4) is also the single-valued normalized entire continuation
of B_M: it is odd and has an exact zero of order2m-1 at zero.
No raw Y value or removable raw J/power phase is being inserted.
Although the present target is positive real(B1), taking absolute
values in(B4) is legitimate even at arbitrary complex z with r=|z|.
Since(gamma)_k>=gamma^k, one gets the global identity-level estimate

 |B_M(z)|<=P(r) exp(x),
 P(r)=pi(r/2)^(2m-1)/[Gamma(M)Gamma(M+1)],
 x=r^2/[4(m+1/2)].                                      (B5)

This exponential is only a scalar absolute-series majorant. It
makes no claim about a matrix norm or the cancellation of a
full-carrier error. No numerical special-function evaluator is used.

## 3. Exact positive Gamma product and a finite factorial bound

 Gamma(M)Gamma(M+1)

      >=pi M [(m-1)!/2^(m-1)]^2.                         (B6)

The inequality uses h-1/2>=h/2 term by term, with no asymptotic
Gamma approximation. For every integer q>=1,

 log(q!)>=integral_1^q log(s)ds=q log q-q+1,
                          q!>=(q/3)^q,                  (B7)
